correctness.rationale: Deutsch–Sagan Theorem 5.2 gives exactly A_r=3K_{r-1}+{-1,0,1}. Disjoint residues modulo 3 prove cardinality. Carry-free K+K digit multiplicities produce all R formulas. The sharp extrema follow from unique all-ones word and characterization of adjacent weights both equal to 1. The cyclic adjacent-weight sum P_m has recurrence P_m=4*6^(m-1)+P_(m-1), and E=19*6^m+8P_m. Compatibility of index-prefix measures and a Bernoulli ternary-digit coupling establish full support, non-atomicity, Haar-singularity, and exact D2. The accompanying finite checker independently enumerated all ordered pairs through r=8 and Catalan values through r=6. Finite verification is explicitly not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Theorem 5.2 in Deutsch–Sagan gives the unit-index digit language but no two-sum distribution; other primary work treats Catalan values or index density. Checked research-record results about single-index 3-adic valuations, Catalan values, unrelated four-adic convolutions and binary additive energies do not cover the exact modular Catalan-unit two-sum fibers. An implicit consequence of a broad digit-automaton convolution theorem remains a documented priority risk, not a demonstrated implication.
residual_risks: A generic theorem on additive convolution of digital Cantor sets could yield the formula as an unstated specialization.
Database searches and inspected sections cannot establish global priority; earlier papers not indexed under Catalan could contain an equivalent.

value.rationale: The exact pair-representation law addresses a natural additive question about the classical Catalan unit-index support and upgrades its known density-zero description into full cyclic additive coverage, all fibers, sharp extrema, exact additive quadruple energy, and full-support singular 3-adic self-convolution. These distinguish additive abundance from measure-theoretic singularity, and the precise coefficients are not supplied by the published one-index congruence theorem.
